items.note: The exchange (X_a,Y_a)->(-Y_a,X_a) with every scratch wire restored, the eight-row schedule and the three stages are stated correctly. But the step calls it a network of 'W linear gates' (W counts wires), and h=100, the triple indexing, the copy/gather/scatter/side maps and the wire counts are missing. The derivation leaves out the key mechanism: the first two rows subtract J a + R c, so the net change (JV+RG)x does not depend on the scratch values (744-750). It also leaves out the stage computation (x,y)->(x,y+x)->(-y,y+x)->(-y,x) (761-763).

The step states the mechanism: a common frame commutes with a pointwise gate, only D_vD_u^{-1} is applied on edges, and the endpoint frames fix the operator. It never gives the operator D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1}, nor the route operator eps_w D_sink(rho(w)) D_source(w)^{-1}. It gives a frame to 'every vertex of a wire' without saying the frame is common to all incidences of a gate. It is one inferred step, not a derivation.

The children state the content correctly: only the central edges from time 3 to 4 decrease, each by h; the budget is Wm-2N+2L; and L/N=100/539 and 101/539. The parent step and its method instead say there is only one decreasing central edge per invocation, which contradicts L=Ich, and L=Ich itself is never written. The method has triple lines and the orthogonality of neighbours. It leaves out the bilinear forms (I-J/9 over Q, the dot product over F_2), the A/B/P/Q stage transitions and the gate-label table (eq:motif-labels).

The endpoint identity M_sink(rho(w))-M_source(w)=I_m, the shear H<-H+D on every role and s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b<W_b m are stated. But the vertex matrices are given only as the projections P_U: the essential source matrix -P_{U_a} at X_a is left out. So are the N source edges of rank one (2P_{U_a}), which is where -N instead of -2N comes from (1162-1167), and the endpoint check P_{U_a^perp}+P_{U_a}=I (1169-1171).

One translation kernel aI+bX_v per orthonormal residual vector, s_c=W_c m-2N+2L_c<W_c m, and C^{tensor m} on every role after corrections all match the paper. The method gives the weight additivity modulo 4 for orthogonal vectors (1232-1257). The endpoint argument is only quoted, not derived: the weight-27 vector u_a, the Z_{a,k} corrections with the scalar i^{27k}, and the negation of the X outputs (1287-1314).

The plan states L/N<1/2, s_b<W_b m, s_c<W_c m, tau=1-2^{-50} and s_b/W_b<m^tau. It gives neither the relative deficits eta_b, eta_c nor the argument from eta>20*2^{-50} and log m<20 that yields s/W<m^tau (1331-1344). The complex bound s_c/W_c<m^sigma appears only in passing in S1.4.6.3.

The O(V) digit moves, splits and merges, the cyclic row split and the controlled shift or scaling are stated. S1.2's claim leaves out the conditions: the prime radix, offsets preparable in b^{O(1)} time, and denominators prime to q. These are only implied by the quoted line. There is no derivation.

The plan states A=E_1 Pi E_2 and exactly a interchanges plus O(V). It shows the paper's route for the shear: triangular factors applied in tape order at linear cost, and each one of Pi realized as D_j<-D_j+H_i, a swap, then D_j<-H_i-D_j. The elimination proof of the factorization (1375-1392) and the choice of the fixed prime q are not shown.

The plan follows the paper's proof: the cyclic row split into W streams of volume V/W, the network with shear frames whose edges are recursive interchanges, the identity D<-D-H, H<-H+D, D<-H-D, the recurrence F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1) with the a<=1 and a>1 cases, and the parking-stack schedule costing O(V) per node.

The plan has the high digits as the row field, padding to R'<2R, base-m pieces and the geometric sum O(Ve^tau). It leaves out how binary chunks are handled, by padding [2^u] to [q^e] with e=O(u) (1721-1734), which is what gives the O(Vu^tau) bound for bit arrays. It also leaves out the choice of rho and the case of unequal widths.

The plan states the conjugation by P_M with one child call per residual vector plus a fixed number of row additions, and H_0^{tensor D}=b^D S_D C^{tensor D} S_D. It leaves out the identity (C^{-1})^{tensor f}=(-i)^f Z C^{tensor f} Z, which makes every child a forward call, and the count of exactly s_c children on e/m axes for a group of e=mf. These are inferred steps only.

The eight rotations, the parity result, the bad set of size at most delta_bad M and the sort-based repair follow the paper. The method never says that each rotation is preceded and followed by chunk swaps that move its target after its controls (2117-2155), which is where the L^tau term comes from. It also leaves out the separate final XOR at j_{f-1} (2187-2193).

Children of volume V/W, F(e)<=(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1), the internal sum O(e^lambda) and the range for lambda' match the paper. Two essential steps are missing: the leaf bound O(a^j u)<=O(e^sigma d^{beta(1-sigma)}) (2421-2430), which is where sigma+beta(1-sigma) comes from, and the bound K<=e^{c/beta} that controls the node overhead. Where the rows come from (the q_0 preprocessed chunks, 2306-2323) is only hinted at.

The plan follows the paper's route: the H_0 layer written through C, the complex network recursion with packed changes of basis, exact evaluation with Delta=ceil(C_0 d^{C_1})=o(p) guard bits from A(e)<=sA(e/m)+E, and one truncation with error <sqrt2 2^{-p}. The proof's check that the packed costs are uniform (2696-2735) is not reproduced.

The plan has omega_t=y^{2r/t}, character cancellation, decimation in frequency with outputs in bit-reversed order (B_tF_t^-, F_t^+B_t^{-1}), rounds grouped as H followed by J_E, the layout by prefix moves and chunk exchanges with their costs, and the error sqrt2 l 2^{-p}, all as in the paper.
Evaluation at B_0=2^{4p} with signed carries, four products with the established multiplier, centred residues using |h_j|<=r2^{2p}<B_0/2, and cost O(rp log(rp)). This is the paper's route.
Retained LB order, the normalization identity, P(LBu,LBv)=LB P(u,v), the error M(3delta+eta) and the cost all follow the proof. The pointwise product's division by r is left implicit in S2.3.

The plan gives the cited Gaussian identity and the estimate on N, inversion by the Neumann series, A=S' and B_0=D'J'C with normalizations multiplying to 2^{-2alpha^2}, the permutations kept rather than sorted, the tensor form and the costs. It does not give the error bound <p^2 for the approximate maps.

Both identities are stated, each with its key reason (the coefficient formula; RF^+R=F^+). The chirp a_j=exp(-pi i sum s_i j_i^2/t_i) is never defined. The commutation of R with pointwise products and the two normalizations are only summarized in inferred steps.

The fixed exponents, the sizes, the axis lengths, alpha and gamma, primes in the two disjoint short intervals from the explicit prime count, T/2<S<T, alpha^4 theta_i>p, and the n^{o(1)} search all match the paper.

Phi is an isomorphism because x maps to an element of order S, the coordinates are triangular, and the map is realized by prefix-controlled cyclic shifts after the axes are reordered, at cost O(Tp d^2(1+l^tau)). This is the paper's route.
The map is well defined, the wrap factor is zeta^{k+l}(-1)^h=zeta^j, and M_C=D_- iota^{-1} M_r(iota D_+ f, iota D_+ g)=(f*g)/T, as in the paper.

The source transform as Gaussian expansion, then chirp by twisted convolution, then compression and rescale, with exact counterpart RF_s; then the six numbered steps with the scales S and 2^{2b+4}S, rounding, Phi^{-1} and carries. All match the paper.

The exact counterpart (u*v)/S^2, E_s=9*2^gamma TL, E_w<28*2^gamma T^2L, the final bound 448b 2^{-b+gamma}<1/2 and the carries are stated. The chain that produces E_s, namely E_ring<5TL and the chirp error <8TL (4591-4650), is skipped.
The table of normalized costs, the margins g_1..g_7, the minimum 2^{-181}=2kappa, logarithms absorbed into p^kappa, and schoolbook multiplication below a cutoff all follow the paper.

S0 concludes that no eventual Omega(n log n) lower bound holds for the machine. It does not spell out the paper's formulation: an eventual bound for every machine, refuted by liminf T_A(n)/(n lg n)=0.

errors.says: Labels can be attached so that only one central-wire edge per invocation decreases, losing h dimensions (the method likewise confines all decreases to one central-wire edge per invocation).
errors.paper: Every central wire's edge from time 3 to 4 decreases. There are c=100 or 101 central wires per invocation, each losing h, so L=Ich (997-1003, 1070-1071). With one decreasing edge per invocation, L would be Ih and L/N would not be 100/539.

errors.says: The projections P_U onto the labels are the vertex matrices, endpoint differences telescope to the identity, and each edge's rank is its change in label dimension.
errors.paper: X_a sources carry -P_{U_a} and other sources carry zero. These N source edges are exceptions with matrix 2P_{U_a} of rank one but no change in dimension, so s_b=W_bm-N+2L_b rather than Wm-2N+2L. The endpoint identity needs -P_{U_a}: P_{U_a^perp}-(-P_{U_a})=I_m (1117-1118, 1162-1171, 1472-1473).

errors.says: A fixed network of W linear gates on wires exchanges two banks of values.
errors.paper: W is the number of wires (eq:bit-wire-count, eq:complex-wire-count; 'Write W for the wire count'). The gates are the schedule rows, at most 12W of them.

errors.says: The opposite transform of the pointwise product, scaled by M, equals (f*g)/(rM).
errors.paper: The identity holds for the normalized pointwise product P(u,v)=uv/r: M F^+((F^-f)(F^-g)/r)=(f*g)/(rM).

chain: The tree follows the paper's route from the two fast tape procedures, through the synthetic transforms, resampling, chirp and CRT, to exact recovery and the cost table, and it reaches O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa}). It thins at the central saving. The parent label step miscounts the decreasing edges. The rank interface leaves out the -P_{U_a} source matrices and their N rank-one exceptions, so its own formula s_b=W_bm-N+2L_b is not explained. The exponent tau=1-2^{-50} is asserted without the eta>20*2^{-50}, log m<20 argument. Further down, the layer recurrence leaves out its leaf bound and exact recovery skips the ring and chirp error stages.

steps.note: The fixed linear network with (X_a,Y_a)->(-Y_a,X_a) and restored scratch wires is stated. But h=100, the data indexed by triples in T^3, N=binom(h,3)^3 and m=h^3 never appear.

S1.3.1.2 has a common frame that commutes with the pointwise gate, edges applying D_vD_u^{-1}, and endpoint frames that fix the net operator. The formula D_out S D_in^{-1} is described in words, not written.

There are nested nondegenerate labels in an m-dimensional space built from triple lines, and S1.3.1.3.1 says the only decreasing edges are the central edges from time 3 to 4, each losing h. The parent step wrongly says there is one such edge per invocation, and F^{tensor 3} is not named.

That rank equals change in dimension appears only in the motivation and method of S1.3.1.4, and the statement that P_V-P_U is the identity on V cap U^perp is not given. The N source edges of rank one, the exceptions, are absent.
Both sum |Delta dim|=Wm-2N+2L (with the telescoping at gates) and s_b=W_bm-N+2L_b are stated. L=Ich is not written, and the step from -2N to -N is left unexplained.
L/N=100/539 and 101/539, both below 1/2, and s_b below W_bm because N-2L_b>0 are stated.
M_sink(rho(w))-M_source(w)=I_m holds for every input role, so the bit network applies the shear (H,D)->(H+D,D) on every role. The source matrix -P_{U_a} that makes this true is left out.
E_1 Pi E_2, exactly a interchanges plus O(V), the one-interchange implementation of each one of Pi, and s recursive calls per node are all present.
Children of volume V/W, F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1), s/W<m^tau with tau=1-2^{-50}, and F_k=O(e^tau) are present. The justification through eta>20*2^{-50} and log m<20 is missing; S1.3.1.5 only asserts it.

central.summary: Seven of the nine steps are reconstructed: frames, labels, the budget, the strict saving, the endpoint identity, edges as recursive calls, and the recurrence. The chain has two gaps. The concrete fixed network (h=100, the triple indexing, N, m) is only alluded to. The rank interface never mentions the -P_{U_a} source matrices and their N rank-one exceptions, which are what turn the budget Wm-2N+2L into s_b=W_bm-N+2L_b and make the endpoint identity hold. The plan also miscounts the decreasing central edges in one step, and it asserts the exponent rather than deriving it from eta.
